estimatedSavingsNotes: DeepTracker schedules one 15-second non-priority batch after eligible work and no longer runs a recurring generic telemetry interval.
Retryable transport failures retain the queue and use a bounded 15/30/60/120-second event-driven backoff while the page is visible.
Pagehide, visibility hidden, cleanup, online, and priority paths retain explicit flush behavior.
Hover and visibility events emit summaries instead of per-transition streams.
Scroll uses requestAnimationFrame and 25/50/75/100 milestones instead of 500ms polling.
Identity link writes pending state before send, then stores success or retry-after state to prevent duplicate bursts.
Runtime request-volume and billing effects remain external evidence; this report makes no provider-cost claim.

fixesApplied.detail: Client telemetry priority remains explicit; non-priority DeepTracker work uses a one-shot 15-second event-triggered batch with a 200-event cap and no recurring generic interval.
Visibility hidden, pagehide, cleanup, and priority closeouts share a route-session closeout key and prefer beacon/keepalive for final sends.
Hover, visibility, and scroll now summarize state; scroll emits only max depth and 25/50/75/100 milestones via requestAnimationFrame.
Identity link submission marks a pending state before fetch, writes a sent state on success, and writes a retry-after window on failure without blocking auth.
